verdicts.quote: Endpoint `POST /tickets/:id/merge`, body `{ "into": "T-0001" }` ... 200 with the duplicate ticket ... or an unknown field is 400 `invalid`.
(`:id` is the duplicate, `into` the surviving ticket).
both tickets exist and are mergeable
verdicts.missing: Whether any duplicate check (same requester, title, priority) is made or the agent's word alone suffices is never stated.

verdicts.quote: now `status: "closed"` and `mergedInto: "<into>"` ... Invariant: a ticket with `mergedInto` is `closed` and the target exists.
verdicts.missing: Whether the merged ticket can afterwards be edited, transitioned or reopened, and what the API answers if tried.

verdicts.quote: The surviving ticket is unchanged (title, priority, status, `updated`). ... (it records the link only: the ticket's own fields stay as they were)
`GET /tickets/:id` of a merged ticket still answers.
verdicts.missing: Whether merged tickets appear in GET /tickets and under status filters is not stated.

verdicts.quote: Failure (409 `conflict`, message names the reason): merging a ticket into itself; a duplicate that is already closed (including already merged); a surviving ticket that is closed.
verdicts.missing: Treatment of tickets in the resolved state (either side) is not decided.

verdicts.quote: unknown `:id` or unknown `into` is 404 `not_found`; body not an object, missing or non-ticket-id `into`, or an unknown field is 400 `invalid`.
verdicts.missing: Which id the error message names, and the answer for a malformed path `:id`.

verdicts.quote: no chains: because closed tickets are refused as a target, a ticket merged into a ticket cannot be merged into a closed one.
verdicts.missing: Whether a survivor that has already absorbed others may itself be merged into another ticket (creating a chain).

verdicts.quote: a duplicate that is already closed (including already merged) ... A refused merge changes nothing ... a refused or repeated merge enqueues nothing.
The surviving ticket is unchanged (title, priority, status, `updated`). ... the surviving ticket gets one entry, action `ticket.merge_received`
any caller naming itself in `X-Actor` (default `system`) may merge ... no authentication or role check is added
a merged ticket reloads with `status`, `mergedInto`, and the audit entries intact. `version` stays 1; a data file written before this change loads unchanged (no `mergedInto` means not merged)
a record whose `mergedInto` is present but not a ticket id, or names no ticket, is refused as a corrupt data file.
verdicts.missing: Whether loading checks cycles and status/link agreement, and the refusal message naming the record.

verdicts.quote: one audit entry on the duplicate, action `ticket.merged`, the request's actor ... the surviving ticket gets one entry, action `ticket.merge_received` ... Visible in `GET /tickets/:id/audit` of each.
a merge is applied atomically in memory (both tickets and the audit entries change in one store call, then one save)
verdicts.missing: Whether the notification is part of the same atomic change, and crash behaviour (before or after, never between).

verdicts.quote: one `ticket.merged` outbox notification to the duplicate's requester, key `ticket.merged:<id>` ... the surviving ticket's requester is not notified
verdicts.missing: What happens to pending notifications about the absorbed ticket; exact template wording.

verdicts.quote: The operators' CLI stays read-only: `show` prints a merged ticket normally and shows `mergedInto` in its details; `list` and `list --raw` columns are unchanged
Preserved: all existing endpoints, ticket fields and lifecycle
`list` and `list --raw` columns are unchanged (the weekly report reads them by position).
verdicts.missing: How absorbed tickets are counted in the weekly report's totals and by-status counts.
